title: Encoder runtime matrix smoke scaffold
summary: Add a synthetic SDR encoder runtime/topology matrix check for descriptor-owned flags without enabling dormant encoder selections.
reason: Encoder breadth/AV1 activation needs runtime evidence before descriptor-backed selection can safely expand. This slice adds a test scaffold that executes CPU descriptor rows through bundled ffmpeg/ffprobe and reports hardware rows as opt-in skips until host-specific validation is requested.
behavior_before: Dormant encoder descriptors had static flag-shape coverage and capability-probe coverage, but no synthetic encode check proving descriptor-built flags could create a video output on the bundled toolchain.
behavior_after: A new PowerShell runtime matrix check generates temporary lavfi media, builds descriptor-owned SDR flags, executes runtime-available CPU descriptor rows, verifies codec output with ffprobe, and skips hardware topology rows by default unless MEDIAPIPELINE_ENCODER_RUNTIME_HARDWARE=1 is set. Active encoder selection and pipeline command generation remain unchanged.

rollback_plan: Remove the new runtime matrix check, revert the docs/test-inventory status updates, and drop this change packet and generated summary updates. No active encoder resolver or media pipeline command behavior is changed.
notes: Hardware descriptor topology execution is intentionally opt-in with MEDIAPIPELINE_ENCODER_RUNTIME_HARDWARE=1 because generic encoder presence does not prove host hardware or descriptor flag readiness. Real-media validation was not run; this is a synthetic SDR scaffold only and does not activate new encoder families or cover HDR preservation.
